decisions.reason: As a core bread line that builds directly on the bakery's established capabilities and shows no visible sign of underperformance, it is likely to remain unless sales clearly disappoint.
The repeated gold medal for the premium raisin stollen is a strong signal that results exceed aspiration levels, making withdrawal very unlikely.
A rye mixed bread with seeds fits current bakery demand and the firm's existing assortment well, so with no negative signal and some industry growth it is likely to be retained.
This darker malted rye variant is somewhat more niche than standard breads, but it still uses the firm's core know-how and there is no evidence of a shortfall severe enough to trigger dropping it.
The marzipan Christmas stollen is close to the firm's confectionery strengths and seasonal range, so it is likely to be kept, though with more uncertainty than the award-winning raisin stollen.

Ancient grain bread is the most experimental of the breads and therefore somewhat more uncertain, but in a growing market and with moderate product-range slack the firm would more likely continue than withdraw it.
